CHAPTER THE FIRST

fast
Once upon a Thursday, under a waxing gibbous moon and the 
sky was clear, this is what happened.
Bought flowers for no one in particular before breakfast.
It was nearly dark by then.
12 days ago: Burned the toast and ate it anyway before breakfast.
Tonight I'm counting everything with a lid. So far it's eleven, and 
one of them is a cat.
Meanwhile, in the Labyrinth…
IN THE LABYRINTH · THE EAST STACKS
The Wrong Castle
The East Stacks grow a tower overnight.
You can see it from the Great Hall windows when the morning 
mist comes off: a thick dark finger standing where the library's 
east wing used to end. The bottom of it is library. I t ' s  g o t  t h e  r i g h t  
stone, the right narrow windows, the right smell of old glue. About 
halfway up, it changes its mind. There's a stretch of grey fortress wall 
with a flag on it that's no flag the Academy owns. And at the very top, 
as if the tower couldn't stop itself, there's a nursery window with 
yellow curtains and a wooden star hanging in the glass.
Between them runs a stair, and the stair keeps asking for another 
floor.
I can hear it from here. It's a slow soft tick, like a clock being wound. 
Each time the stair asks, the tower takes a stone from somewhere else 
and says yes.

THE TALE OF YOUR WEEK THURSDAY 22 OCTOBER · CONTINUED
— 5 · NTK6 —
A drawbridge hangs down over the Quillquarium. The nibs under-
neath are in a state. They've never agreed so completely, all thousand 
of them, in one long furious scribble, and the noise of it comes up 
through the floor like bees in a wall.
I've read about a tower like this one. It was in a book, and the book 
was careful, and the tower stayed in the book. It wasn't supposed to 
get out.
Penny's pinning up a notice on the foot of the stair. She does it with a 
drawing-pin and quite a lot of dignity:
THE EAST STACKS ARE SEVERAL PLACES. PLEASE USE ONE AT A 
TIME.
Permancer is tying ribbons to the banister, one at every third post, in 
a pattern he's clearly worked out on paper. Wicker is holding the 
source volume, the old black copy of Dracula, open at the page, closed 
over his finger. He holds it like a man who's been handed a baby by an 
enemy. Serenity is studying her map.
It's been thirteen days since the East Stacks. She's gone back to her 
work. She's gone back to toast. She's lost no weight in the face and 
gained no softness, and on her neck, above the collar, there's a thin 
line that isn't quite scar and isn't quite not. She looks up from her 
map, and across the hall at the tower, and the corner of her mouth 
goes in.
“I'm coming,” she says.
“I was about to ask,” says Permancer.
“You're very slow.”
“I'm very thorough.”
“That's what I said.”
She folds the map into her repaired case. It's the mended one, with 
the small crooked clasp. I watch the clasp click shut under her thumb, 
a clean small snick, a n d  I  w a t c h  W i c k e r ,  a c r o s s  t h e  h a l l ,  w a t c h  i t  
happen. He watches it the way you'd watch a bridge you've built take 
weight for the first time.
She catches him looking.
She doesn't smile. She doesn't scowl. She gives him a small, level nod,

THE TALE OF YOUR WEEK THURSDAY 22 OCTOBER · CONTINUED
— 6 · GD36 —
just a fraction of an inch, the kind you give to a stranger who's held a 
door. Then she goes ahead.
Permancer counts us at the doorway. He counts twice, now. He's 
started to count a third time, and he stops himself, and just holds the 
bookmark a moment longer than he needs to, and nobody says 
anything.
Inside, the stair turns into a corridor. It's a long one, lamplit, with a 
floor of old boards and, beyond a bend, three ways through.
I tie my ribbon to the doorframe behind us. It's the only thing I can 
do. It's the end I've got, and I leave it fluttering there like a flag on a 
very small ship, so that, whatever else happens, we'll be able to find 
the way out.
you chose · The ballroom.
The Wrong Castle
Dracula's waiting in the central hall.
It's a great high round room, built out of several different castles, and 
none of them has agreed to hold it up. The ceiling's from one place. 
The floor's from another. A fireplace in the north wall is blowing 
snow into the room, sideways, in long clean ribbons, and it's settling 
on the Count's coat. Above him, the stolen nursery window has 
swung in on its own wall, and is trying very hard to find morning.
“This is not my castle,” he says.
He sounds, for the first time, uncertain. He sounds like a man stand-
ing in somebody else's kitchen.
“No,” says Serenity. “These are everybody else's rooms.”
She's got her map in both hands, and her chin up.
A door opens in the east wall, and through it there's a small boat in a 
great storm, the whole sea heaving past the frame. Permancer throws 
himself at the handle and drags it shut, and a quart of seawater goes 
through the gap and soaks him to the knees.
“You have damaged my source,” says Dracula.
There's no heat in it. It's an accusation said very quietly, with a

THE TALE OF YOUR WEEK THURSDAY 22 OCTOBER · CONTINUED
— 7 · AVG4 —
certain regret, by a man who's found his house wrecked and isn't sure 
whose fault it is.
Permancer keeps both hands on the handle. He's wet and he's tired 
and for once he's not lecturing.
“We did,” he says.
It's a big thing, to say. I feel it go through the room. Nobody's expect-
ing it, least of all the Count.
Wicker's holding the source volume open. He's standing very still, his 
shoulders drawn in, looking down at the page. His own sentence is 
there, in his own hand. For one sentence, let him choose the verb.  A n d  
under it, in a second hand, small and neat, one word:
FOLLOW .
“I thought—” Wicker begins.
Serenity waits. She doesn't help him. She just waits.
He looks at the map case, with its crooked clasp. At the bandage 
above it, half hidden by her collar. He looks, I think, at everything he's 
ever made go wrong.
“I wanted to see what would happen.”
“You have,” says Serenity.
It's not cruel. It's perfectly level. He takes it. He lowers his eyes to the 
page and, for the first time since the Jump, doesn't look away.
Then the wall splits.
It happens quietly. There's a long thin crack, as if a very big breath 
has been let out behind the plaster, and where the stone parts there's 
something white. It's a fold of paper. A single sheet, thin as a held 
breath, running up the wall like ivy.
I know that paper.
I'd know it in the dark. I'd know it from across the Labyrinth. It's the 
same stuff I'm made of: the same flax, the same lime, the same long 
slow soak in a vat. It's paper. It's a page. And there's a gap in the page, 
a narrow clean tear like the one in the corner of a bookplate, and cold 
air's coming through it, and through the cold I can hear s o m e t h i n g .  
It's very far off. It sounds like a cover being opened.

THE TALE OF YOUR WEEK THURSDAY 22 OCTOBER · CONTINUED
— 8 · 3FW3 —
Serenity touches the fold with one finger. Her map pulls toward the 
gap in her hands, the whole sheet stretching toward it like a plant.
“His way back,” she says.
Permancer brings the bookmark near. Its ribbons lift, one by one, and 
reach across the hall toward the source volume in Wicker's hands, 
toward the tear in the wall, and, slowly, almost reluctantly, toward 
Serenity.
Penny's already got three cards out. She sets one beside each, with a 
click.
SOURCE. INVITATION. LIVING CLAIM.
Dracula watches her write. His face doesn't move.
Serenity looks at the third card. It lies on the flagstone by her foot, 
plain white, with her own name nowhere on it. Then she puts out her 
hand, flat, and covers it.
“That one's mine.”
Behind us, through the shut door, the sea knocks again.

keptPages.text:
I tried the thing from the Wayfinding class, mapping the street by smell, on the way home. Bakery, then the laundrette (hot cotton), then the bins behind the chip shop, then nothing for a long stretch, then woodsmoke from somebody's chimney two roads over. I'd never have noticed the woodsmoke if I hadn't been playing. I stood at the corner for a while just breathing it in like a weirdo.

I think that's what this whole Book is for, honestly. Making me stand on corners.
